AMBIENT WATCH LOOP triggers - edit to opt in, no code changes needed.

Each trigger has:
  id        - unique name (appears in var/logs/tasks.jsonl as watch:<id>)
  goal      - the goal string, planned through L4 (one LLM call per distinct
              goal per daemon run, then cached) OR
  plan      - an inline deterministic plan dict (no LLM; must be fully
              resolved - no $facts refs)
  schedule  - {"type": "time", "at": "HH:MM", "days": ["mon"...]} fires once
              per day after the time; {"type": "file", "directory": ...,
              "name": <substring>, "recursive": bool} fires once per new
              matching file
  enabled   - false means the trigger is inert; set true to activate
  notify    - send a desktop notification when the trigger finishes (default true)
  allow     - OPTIONAL primitive allowlist: a list of exact names or 'mod.*'
              patterns. If present, any plan step whose primitive is NOT on
              the list is REFUSED before execution (recorded as REFUSED,
              never executed) - for unattended triggers whose LLM plan must
              be constrained, e.g. "allow": ["gmail.*"] (L2 verify checks
              are read-only and always permitted).

The gmail trigger below is ENABLED (wired in): its goal references
$facts.gmail_sender, so the sender is edited in config/planner_facts.json,
not in the trigger. An empty mailbox for that sender is an honest FAIL
(never an error) - if you do not reliably receive unread mail from
accounts.google.com, change gmail_sender in planner_facts.json.
The weekly-cross-project-digest trigger is ENABLED (Phase C v2.2): a DETERMINISTIC plan (no L4 LLM call) that gathers git.log from Friday + vivaha + Aether, discovers each repo's most recently modified status/planning doc (files.find_recent_doc: PLAN_STATUS/ROADMAP/DEVLOG/STATUS/TODO/CHANGELOG shapes, README fallback - no hand-maintained note), reads those docs, then calls dev.digest - the ONE live full-tier LLM call (~$0.17/run), once per week on Sundays at 10:00. Repo paths are hardcoded here (deterministic plans must be fully resolved); edit them if the repos move. Its allow list is exactly the gather/synthesize/verify/deliver primitives (git.log, files.find_recent_doc, files.read_text, dev.digest, digestcheck.verify_attribution, notify.notify_send), so the plan can never reach for anything side-effecting. The digest text is delivered to the desktop as the final notify.notify_send step's body. The plan now discovers each repo's status doc by RECENCY (files.find_recent_doc, no hand-maintained note) and runs digestcheck.verify_attribution on the digest before delivery - the v2.1 provenance-confabulation fix, made mechanical (verdict in PHASE_C_V2_PROOF.md). Agent-Reach is deliberately NOT included (third-party, not Lakshay's); Psyche Space and ChangelogAI are excluded pending a separate decision. The `sunday-digest-reminder` trigger is ENABLED (Sundays 10:05, 5 minutes after the digest): a one-step deterministic notify-only plan (allow ["notify.notify_send"], notify:false so it does not double-ping) that nudges Lakshay to log his weekly verdict in gates/DIGEST_TRACKING.md - the human judgment the digest's mechanical checks cannot render.
The two `ambient-gap-probe-*` triggers (11:00 and 11:05 daily, enabled) are the DELIBERATE ambient volume source for the self-improvement loop: each is a silent (notify:false), allowlisted deterministic probe whose single step is a genuinely UNBUILT primitive (calendar.list_upcoming, gmail.send_document). The allowlist refuses the step BEFORE any execution - nothing ever runs, zero side effects - and REFUSED is terminal-for-the-day, so each probe records exactly ONE real capability-gap record per day for triage to group and LLM-draft (the first real ambient proposals, exercising volume + draft quality).The gap
count in the daemon.alive heartbeat now rises ~2/day - that rise is the intended signal,
not noise; consume via gap_triage + the approval gate, never by weakening the allowlist.
LIFECYCLE: once a probe's primitive is approved and registered, RETIRE the probe (disable
it or repoint it at the next unbuilt surface) - its daily refusal of a now-solved
primitive is noise (gap_triage consumes such gaps without drafting, but the file still
grows). Approving the email-send probe's proposal also expands Friday's gmail surface
RETIRED 2026-08-11: gmail.send_document was hand-built, gated, human-signed and registered (the loop's first side-effecting primitive), so ambient-gap-probe-email-send is now DISABLED per this lifecycle. The morning-gmail-summary allowlist was TIGHTENED from 'gmail.*' to the three read-only primitives (gmail.list_unread / gmail.get_message / gmail.summarize) so the LLM-planned morning trigger can never reach the send primitive. The calendar probe remains enabled (calendar.list_upcoming is still unbuilt).
ADDED 2026-08-13: ambient-gap-probe-file-write - a THIRD deliberate probe (daily 00:05) whose
single step is files.write_text (a WRITE-capable files.* primitive - genuinely unbuilt, the files
module is read-only today: find_file/find_file_exact/find_recent_doc/read_text). It is the one
probe whose class (files.*) HAS a real build-verify stage - the gate's documented READ-family
limit means a write-primitive draft is expected to be rejected there ('deliberate and visible in
the report'). FIRST RUN 2026-08-13: the LLM draft was caught EARLIER, at contract-schema stage
(4-segment name 'friday.l1.files.write_notes', invalid decorator syntax, primitive renamed to
write_notes) - never reached AST/sandbox/build-verify. Its rejected-draft dir is COMPLETE, so
triage now consumes daily files.write_text gaps WITHOUT re-drafting (tombstone behavior): if the
probe stays enabled it adds one consumed gap/day - decide explicitly whether to keep it as
ambient volume, retire it, or hand-correct the draft and re-run the gate. Its allowlist refuses
the step before any execution (zero side effects), notify:false, REFUSED is terminal-for-the-day
- exactly one gap record per day, same lifecycle as the calendar probe: retire this probe if
files.write_text is ever approved and registered.
from read-only to side-effecting - a deliberate trust decision.  Safety is inherited from the core: the executor refuses blocked primitives,
window close never touches protected classes, and dev.run_shell needs
FRIDAY_ALLOW_DANGEROUS=1. Triggers run strictly one at a time.

Run once (for cron / testing):  ./.venv/bin/python -m friday.watcher --once
Run as a daemon:               ./.venv/bin/python -m friday.watcher --poll 30

RETIRED 2026-08-13: ambient-gap-probe-file-write DISABLED - files.write_text was approved and registered through the FULL self-improvement loop (refusal -> gap -> self-checked LLM draft -> automated gate AST/sandbox/write-family-build-verify -> human review -> register). The probe's job is done; any remaining files.write_text gaps are consumed as SOLVED by triage. Lifecycle precedent: email-send probe.
RETIRED 2026-08-13: ambient-gap-probe-calendar DISABLED - calendar.list_upcoming was registered through the loop's second complete cycle (self-checked LLM draft, automated gate with build-verify honestly NOT APPLICABLE for the calendar class, human-signed) with ZERO hand-correction. Note: it needs calendar OAuth creds (pass friday/calendar or GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TOKEN) to return real events; without them it returns [] and the probe's original goal fails verification honestly.
